title: A network with hubs
caption: In a network, nodes are molecules and edges are interactions. The number of connections of a node is its degree. In a scale-free network most nodes have few connections and a few hubs have many. This one is simulated by adding each new node to a network with a preference for nodes that already have many links; many biological networks look like this, which is why removing a hub (as with p53 in the lesson) can disrupt so much.
alt: A network of 36 circles joined by lines, with a few large orange hubs each joined to many small blue circles. A bar chart on the right shows many nodes with 2 or 3 links and a long tail up to the largest hub.
description: Nodes are molecules; edges are interactions.
Degree: the number of connections of a node.
Hubs are highly connected nodes; most nodes have few links.
Simulated by preferential attachment: not real interaction data.
